p0.original: 关键问题：认知心理学如何解释学习
p0.en: Key issue: How cognitive psychology interprets learning

p2.original: 在认知心理学看来，某些形式的学习只能解释为心理过程的改变，而不仅仅是行为本身的改变。
p2.en: In cognitive psychology, certain forms of learning can only be interpreted as changes in the psychological process, not just changes in behaviour itself.

p3.original: 生物学家J. D.沃森（Watson，1968）在《双螺旋》（The Double Helix）中这样描述，他和弗朗西斯·克里克（Francis Crick）在几个月的反复试错后，他们在某天的灵机一动中破解了遗传密码。在解决自己的问题时，你可能也有类似的突然的（虽说可能不那么出名的）灵机一动，也许那时你对这个问题已经研究了一段时间，然后突然之间，解决方案就清晰起来。这样的事件让严格的行为主义者难以自圆其说，因为它们显然涉及学习，却很难用巴甫洛夫或斯金纳的条件反射来解释。
p3.en: The biologist, J. D. Watson, 1968, described it in The Double Helix, who, after several months of repeated error, and Francis Crick, broke the genetic code in the actuator of one day. You may have a similar sudden (though not so famous) impulse to solve your own problems, and maybe you've been working on this for some time, and suddenly the solution becomes clear. Such incidents make it difficult for strictists to justify themselves, because they are clearly about learning, but they are difficult to interpret with a reflection of Pavlov or Skinner conditions.

p4.original: 许多心理学家认为，一个被称为认知学习的完全不同的过程是产生这种灵机一动的原因。从认知的角度来看，学习并不总是立即表现在行为中。相反，学习可以仅仅反映在心理活动中，正如本节的核心概念：
p4.en: Many psychologists believe that an entirely different process, known as cognitive learning, is the cause of this dynamic. From a cognitive point of view, learning is not always immediately manifested in behaviour. On the contrary, learning can be reflected only in psychological activities, as is the core concept of this section:

p5.original: 在认知心理学看来，某些形式的学习只能解释为心理过程的改变，而不仅仅是行为本身的改变。
p5.en: In cognitive psychology, certain forms of learning can only be interpreted as changes in the psychological process, not just changes in behaviour itself.

p6.original: 让我们看看认知心理学家如何探查学习背后的内隐的心理过程。为此，我们先带你前往北非海岸附近的加那利群岛。
p6.en: Let's see how cognitive psychologists look at the underlying psychological processes behind learning. To that end, we will first take you to the Canary Islands near the North African coast.

p14.original: 描述科勒如何发现顿悟学习。
p14.en: I'm not sure if I'm going to be able to do this, but I'm not going to do it.

p15.original: 格式塔心理学家沃尔夫冈·科勒（Wolfgang Köhler）在第一次世界大战期间被困在特内里费岛上，花了很多时间苦思冥想学习的机制。科勒对于行为主义者对学习的解释不再抱有幻想，试图发展出自己的理论。在他看来，心理学必须承认心理过程是学习的重要组成部分，即使心理事件早已被行为主义者视为主观推测而被唾弃。为了证明他的观点，科勒利用德国政府在特内里费岛建造的灵长类动物研究的相关设施。在那里，他基于可观察的行为设计了实验，旨在揭示认知学习的可测量要素（Sharps & Wertheimer，2000；Sherrill，1991）。
p15.en: The form tower psychologist Wolfgang Köhler was trapped on Tenerife Island during the First World War and spent a lot of time thinking about mechanisms for meditation. Kool no longer fantasies about the behavioral interpretation of learning and tries to develop his own theory. In his view, psychology must acknowledge that the psychological process is an important part of learning, even though psychological events have long been rejected as subjective speculations by activists. In support of his point of view, Koehler made use of facilities for primate research built by the Government of Germany on Tenerife Island. There, he designed experiments based on observable behaviour aimed at revealing measurable elements of cognitive learning (Sharps & Wertheimer, 2000); Sherrill, 1991.

p16.original: 在一系列著名的研究中，科勒发现黑猩猩可以去学习解决复杂的问题，不仅仅是通过反复试错（行为主义者喜欢的一种解释），而是通过“灵机一动”将先前学过的一些更简单的反应组合起来。在其中一个实验中，黑猩猩“苏丹”已经学会了把箱子堆叠起来、爬上去拿悬挂在高处的水果，也学会了用棍子去拿够不着的水果。科勒向苏丹展示一个结合了这两种问题的新情境，即水果悬挂在更高的空中。这时，黑猩猩首先以试错的方式来尝试，用棍子来够它，但没有成功。然后，苏丹似乎很沮丧，扔掉了木棍，踢了踢墙，坐了下来。据科勒报告，这只动物随后挠了挠头，开始盯着它附近的一些箱子。似乎是经过一段时间的“思考”，它突然跳起来，将一只箱子和一根棍子拖到水果下面，爬上箱子，用棍子敲下了他的奖品（见图4-9）。
p16.en: In a series of well-known studies, Koehler found that chimpanzees can learn to solve complex problems, not only through repeated error (an explanation preferred by behaviouralists), but rather by combining some of the simpler responses previously learned through “mixers”. In one of these experiments, the chimpanzee “Sudan” has learned to stack up boxes, climb up to get the high-seasoned fruit, and to get the unreachable fruit with a stick. Kool has shown the Sudan a new context in which both issues are combined, namely, that the fruits are hanging higher in the air. The chimpanzees then tried to fill it with sticks in the wrong way, but failed. The Sudan then appeared to be depressed, throwing out sticks, kicking the wall and sitting down. According to Koller, the animal then scratched his head and started staring at some boxes near it. It seems to have been “thinking” for some time, and it jumped off, dragged a box and a stick under the fruit, climbed up the box and knocked down his prize with a stick (see figures 4-9).

p18.original: 注：科勒的黑猩猩所表现出的那种学习行为，与行为主义者的经典条件反射和操作性条件反射的解释相悖。在本图中，你会看到科勒最聪明的黑猩猩苏丹通过堆叠箱子并爬到箱子上来解决够不着香蕉的问题。科勒声称苏丹的行为证明了顿悟学习。
p18.en: Note: The behaviour of the chimpanzee in Kool is contrary to the behavior of the behaviorists in the classic reflection of conditions and the interpretation of operational conditions. In this figure, you can see that the smartest chimpanzee in Kolle is Sudan that can't solve the problem of bananas by stacking boxes and climbing them. Kool claims that the conduct of the Sudan is proof of the need to learn.

p19.original: 不同寻常的是，苏丹以前从未见过或使用过这样的反应组合。科勒认为，这种行为证明动物不仅会无意识地使用条件反应，而且会通过顿悟来学习，即重新组织它们对问题的感知。他大胆提议，这种行为表明猿类可以像人类一样通过突然感知到新形式或关系中熟悉的物体来学习解决问题，这明显属于心理过程，而不仅是行为过程。他称之为顿悟学习（Köhler，1925）。科勒说，顿悟学习（insight learning）源于对情境感知方式的突然重组。
p19.en: It is unusual that the Sudan has never seen or used such a combination of reactions before. According to Koehler, this behaviour proves that animals not only are unwittingly responding to conditions, but also learn through awareness, i.e. by reorganizing their perception of the problem. He boldly suggested that such behaviour showed that apes could learn to solve problems by suddenly learning, as humans do, about new forms or familiar objects in relationships, which were clearly psychological processes, not just behavioural processes. He calls it Köhler, 1925. Kool said that insight learning had resulted from a sudden reorganization of situational awareness.

p20.original: 行为主义无法令人信服地解释科勒的示例。无论是经典条件反射还是操作性条件反射都无法用刺激和反应来解释苏丹的行为。因此，科勒的黑猩猩的这些壮举需要通过知觉重组来进行认知解释。
p20.en: Activism cannot convincingly explain Kole's example. Neither the classic reflexes nor the operational reflexes can be interpreted as stimuli or reactions to the Sudan's behaviour. Therefore, these efforts by the chimpanzees in Kool need to be explained in a cognitive manner.

p21.original: 4.9 认知地图：托尔曼发现大鼠在想什么
p21.en: 4.9 Cognition map: Tolman found out what rats were thinking.

p23.original: 审视爱德华·托尔曼关于认知地图和潜在学习的实验如何挑战已有的行为理论。
p23.en: Consider how Edward Torman's experiments on cognitive maps and potential learning challenge existing behavioural theories.

p24.original: 在科勒用黑猩猩进行实验后不久，加州大学伯克利分校的爱德华·托尔曼（Edward Tolman）实验室中的大鼠也开始表现出与公认的行为学说背道而驰的行为。它们会穿过实验室迷宫，就像它们头脑中存在一幅迷宫“地图”一样，而不是无脑地执行一系列习得的行为。让我们看看托尔曼如何设法展示这些“有脑”反应。
p24.en: Shortly after Corle was experimenting with chimpanzees, rats at Edward Tolman's laboratory at the University of California in Berkeley also began to demonstrate behaviour contrary to accepted behavioural doctrines. They will pass through the lab maze, just as there is a maze in their minds “maps”, rather than carrying out a whole range of practices unwittingly. Let's see how Tolman managed to show these brain reactions.

p26.original: 只要你曾经在黑暗的家中走动过，就会知道托尔曼所说的“认知地图”是什么意思。确切而言，认知地图（cognitive map）是生物体用来在熟悉的环境中导航的心理意象。但是，像大鼠这样头脑简单的生物也会有如此复杂的心理意象吗？如果是，如何证明这些认知地图的存在？托尔曼认为，大鼠在通往目标的首选路径被阻塞时能够在迷宫中快速选择替代路线，如果要解释这种现象，认知地图是唯一的方式。事实上，大鼠经常会选择绕过障碍物的最短绕行路线，即使这条特定路线以前从未被强化过。托尔曼的大鼠不是（像行为理论所预测的那样）通过反复试错盲目地探索迷宫的不同部分，而是表现得他们好像对迷宫有一个心理表征（图4-10显示了这样一个迷宫的布局）。
p26.en: As long as you've been walking through the dark home, you know what Torman means by “cognitive maps”. To be precise, cognition map (cognition map) is the psychological image used by organisms to navigate in a familiar environment. But would a simple mind like a rat have such a complex psychological image? If so, how can the existence of these cognitive maps be proved? According to Torman, rats are able to quickly select alternative routes in the maze when their preferred path to the target is blocked, and cognitive maps are the only way to explain this. In fact, rats often choose to bypass the shortest bypass route of the barrier, even though this particular route has never been reinforced before. Tolman rats are not (as predicted by the behavior theory) searching blindly for different parts of the labyrinth through repeated attempts, but they are acting as if they had a psychological expression of the maze (figures 4-10 show the layout of such a maze).

p27.original: 图4-10 在迷宫学习中使用认知地图
p27.en: Figure 4-10 Use of cognitive maps in maze learning

p28.original: 注：本实验中使用的大鼠在直线路径开放时更喜欢直线路径（路径1）。当路径1在A处被阻塞时，大鼠更喜欢路径2。当路径2在B处被阻塞时，大鼠通常选择路径3。大鼠的行为表明它们有一张指示了通往食盒的最佳路线的认知地图。
p28.en: Note: The rats used in this experiment prefer straight paths (path 1) when they are open. When path 1 is blocked at A, rats prefer path 2. When path 2 is blocked at B, rats usually select path 3. The rats' behaviour indicates that they have a cognitive map indicating the best route to the food box.

p29.original: 托尔曼提出学习不仅是行为上的，也是心理上的，为了进一步支持这个论断，他做了另一个实验：在大鼠学会跑迷宫后，他在迷宫中放水，结果表明大鼠完全有能力游过迷宫。这再次证明了动物学到的是一个概念，而不仅仅是行为。托尔曼认为，大鼠不仅学会了一系列的左转右转，还形成了对迷宫空间布局更抽象的心理表征（Tolman & Honzik，1930；Tolman et al.，1946）。
p29.en: Tolman argued that learning was not only behavioural, but also psychological, and to further support that assertion, he did another experiment: after rats learned to run the maze, he put water in the maze, which showed that rats were perfectly capable of swimming through the maze. This proves once again that animals learn a concept, not just behavior. According to Torman, rats learn not only a series of left-right turns, but also a more abstract psychological representation of the maze space layout (Tolman & Honzik, 1930; Tolman et al., 1946.

p31.original: 在抨击行为主义基础的另一项研究中，托尔曼（1948）允许他的大鼠在迷宫中自由游荡数小时。在此期间，大鼠只是探索迷宫，而没有得到任何奖赏。然而，尽管缺乏行为学家认为迷宫学习所不可或缺的强化，但是这些大鼠也比其他从未见过这个迷宫的大鼠更快地学会了跑迷宫以获得食物奖赏。很明显，它们在探索时期就学习了迷宫的布局，尽管它们当时的行为看不出任何学习的迹象。托尔曼称之为潜在学习。
p31.en: In another study critical of the basis of behaviorism, Torman (1948) allowed his rat to wander freely in the labyrinth for hours. In the meantime, rats were merely exploring the maze without receiving any reward. However, despite the lack of behaviouralists who consider maze learning to be an indispensable reinforcement, the rats have learned to run the maze more quickly than any other rat that has never seen it in order to obtain food rewards. It is clear that they learned the layout of the maze during the exploration period, although their behaviour at the time did not reveal any signs of learning. Tolman called it a potential study.

p32.original: 4.9.3 托尔曼研究工作的重要意义
p32.en: 4.9.3 Importance of the Tolman Research Work

p33.original: 与科勒的实验一样，托尔曼的工作之所以重要且具有颠覆性，是因为它挑战了巴甫洛夫、华生和其他行为主义者的主流观点。虽然托尔曼接受心理学必须研究可观察行为的观点，但他证明了刺激和反应之间的简单关联并不能解释他在实验中观察到的行为。因此，托尔曼的认知解释严重挑战了行为主义（Gleitman，1991）。
p33.en: Like Kool, the work of Tolman is important and subversive because it challenges the dominant views of Pavlov, Watson and other activists. Although Torman accepted the view that psychology had to study observable behaviour, he proved that the simple link between irritation and reaction did not explain the behaviour he had observed in the experiment. Thus, the cognitive interpretation of Tolman seriously challenged behaviorism (Gleitman, 1991).

p34.original: 随后对大鼠、黑猩猩和人类的认知地图进行的实验广泛地支持了托尔曼的工作（Olton，1992）。最近的脑成像研究指出，海马是大脑中参与“绘制”认知地图的结构（Jacobs & Schenk，2003）。因此，托尔曼的论断似乎是正确的：生物体通过探索来学习其环境的空间布局，即使没有因探索而得到强化，它们也会这样做。从进化角度看，生成认知地图的能力对于必须觅食的动物的来说具有高度的适应性（Kamil et al.，1987）。也许这就是为什么我们会如此迅速地发展出绘制认知地图的能力。
p34.en: The subsequent experiments on cognitive maps of rats, chimpanzees and humans extensively supported Torman's work (Olton, 1992). A recent study of brain imaging indicates that the hippos are the structures involved in “mapping” cognitive maps in the brain (Jacobs & Schenk, 2003). Thus, Tolman's assertion seems correct: organisms learn the spatial configuration of their environment through exploration, and they do so even if they are not reinforced by exploration. From an evolutionary perspective, the ability to produce cognitive maps is highly adaptable to animals that must feed (Kamil et al., 1987). Maybe that's why we're developing so quickly the capacity to produce cognitive maps.

p35.original: 图中的鸟叫作“克拉克的胡桃夹子”，这种鸟是认知地图的惊人示例。每年夏天，它们都会在大峡谷的地下埋藏多达30000个松子和种子。在接下来的冬天，它们可以找到其中的90%，尽管白雪覆盖的冬季景观有所不同。
p35.en: The bird in the picture is called "Clark's walnut clamps" and it's an amazing example of a cognitive map. Every summer, they bury up to 30,000 pines and seeds in the ground of the Grand Canyon. Over the next winter, they can find 90 per cent of them, although snow covers different winter landscapes.

p36.original: 4.10 观察学习：班杜拉对行为主义的挑战
p36.en: 4.10 Observe learning: Bandura's challenge to behaviorism

p38.original: 描述班杜拉对我们理解学习的贡献。
p38.en: Describe Bandura's contribution to our understanding of learning.

p39.original: 另一位著名的心理学家阿尔伯特·班杜拉（Albert Bandura）追随托尔曼的脚步，推翻了行为主义的另一个重要观点：奖惩只对受到奖惩的个体起作用。班杜拉指出，即便我们只是看到别人得到奖赏和惩罚，奖赏和惩罚也可以有效地改变我们自己的行为。（这就是赌场大力宣传头奖得主的原因。）班杜拉的工作表明，行为的后果可以通过观察来间接发挥作用。他的主张为行为学习领域提供了另一个认知成分。让我们看看他是如何证明这个想法的。
p39.en: Another famous psychologist, Albert Bandura, followed Torman's footsteps and reversed another important view of behaviorism: rewards and punishments only work for individuals who are rewarded and punished. Bandura notes that even if we see others being rewarded and punished, rewards and penalties can effectively change our own behaviour. (That's why the casinos are promoting the winners of the prize. The work of Bandura shows that the consequences of behaviour can work indirectly by observing. His ideas provide another cognitive component in the field of behavioural learning. Let's see how he proves it.

p40.original: 1961年，电视的迅速兴起促使阿尔伯特·班杜拉开始研究他的一个猜测：观察暴力行为是否会使观众更有可能变得有暴力倾向？当时流行的观点是，通过观看暴力可以消除观众对攻击性的需求，实际上减少了其攻击性倾向。然而，班杜拉质疑这种想法，他邀请儿童和成年人到他在斯坦福大学的实验室进行一个简单的实验。成年人被带入一个房间里，里面有各种各样的玩具，包括一个波波娃娃（一个底部有重量的充气塑料小丑）。一些成年人（在进入房间之前）被指示通过击打、踢打和拳打来攻击娃娃。其他成年人被指示在房间里温和安静地玩耍。每个孩子都会接触一个成年人，之后在房间里单独玩耍。孩子们做了什么？你猜对了——他们会模仿他们看到的成年人所做的事情，无论是攻击性行为，还是温和行为（Bandura et al.，1963）。随后的研究显示了类似的结果：儿童会模仿他们在电视或电子游戏中看到的攻击性行为，相比处于控制状态的儿童，他们表现出七倍的攻击性行为——即使榜样只是卡通人物（Anderson et al.，2007；Boyatzis et al.，1995）。
p40.en: In 1961, the rapid rise of television prompted Albert Bandura to begin studying his guess: Will observing violence make the audience more likely to be violent? The prevailing view at the time was that the demand for aggressiveness by viewing violence could be eliminated and, in fact, its aggressive orientation reduced. However, Bandura questioned this idea and invited children and adults to a simple experiment in his laboratory at Stanford University. Adults were brought into a room with toys of all kinds, including a Bopo doll (a heavy plastic clown at the bottom). Some adults (before entering the room) were instructed to attack dolls by beating, kicking and punching. Other adults were instructed to play in a gentle and quiet manner in the room. Every child is exposed to an adult and then plays alone in the room. What did the kids do? You're right - they'll imitate what they see as adults, whether it's offensive or moderate (Bandura et al., 1963). Subsequent studies have shown similar results: children can imitate offensive behaviour they see on television or in video games, and they display seven times more aggressive behaviour than children in control, even if role models are mere cartoon characters (Anderson et al., 2007); Boyatzis et al., 1995.

p42.original: 因此，学习不仅可以通过直接经验进行，还可以通过观察另一个人或榜样的行为来进行。如果榜样的行为看起来很成功，或者说，如果榜样似乎得到了奖赏，那么我们可能就会以同样的方式行事。如此一来，通过观察和模仿来学习其实是操作性条件反射的延伸：我们观察到其他人获得奖赏会影响我们的行为，就好像我们自己也获得了奖赏。
p42.en: Thus, learning can take place not only through direct experience, but also by observing the behaviour of another individual or example. If the role models appear successful, or if they seem to be rewarded, then we may act in the same way. So, learning through observation and imitation is actually an extension of the reflection of operational conditions: we observe that other people receive rewards that affect our behaviour, as if we have received a reward ourselves.

p43.original: 这个男孩模仿了他所见过的一个成年人的攻击行为。
p43.en: The boy imitated an adult attack he had seen.

p44.original: 心理学家将此称为社会学习或观察学习（observational learning）。它解释了儿童会模仿看起来成功的、令人钦佩的或似乎自得其乐的攻击性行为的榜样，通过模仿来学习攻击性行为。观察学习也解释了许多其他行为：我们如何学习运动技能、如何驾驶汽车、如何与朋友相处，以及在工作面试中又要有哪些不同的表现。它还影响着我们所遵循的时尚，以及俚语表达的迅速传播。我们模仿我们钦佩的人，希望获得我们认为他们所获得的“奖赏”，无论是地位、认同、钦佩还是其他东西。
p44.en: Psychologists refer to this as social learning or observational learning. It explains that children learn offensive behaviour by imitating examples of aggressive behaviour that appear successful, admirable or seemingly self-excusable. Observation learning also explains many other behaviours: how we learn sports skills, how to drive cars, how to spend time with friends, and how to behave differently in job interviews. It also affects the fashion we follow, as well as the rapid spread of the slang language. We imitate those whom we admire and want to get what we think they have received, whether it be status, identity, admiration or something.

p45.original: 观察学习也发生在非人类物种中，就像母猫教她的小猫如何捕猎一样。事实上，动物为生存而必须做出的许多重要决定——例如，吃什么食物、要避免什么天敌以及如何找到水——都依赖于观察学习。这种类型的学习可以让幼小的动物不需要潜在致命的试错期就能发展出有效的行为。黑猩猩和乌鸦都会学习使用树叶和树枝来制作便于挖掘幼虫和蚂蚁的工具。事实上，无论是人类还是非人类，许多动物的行为都是观察学习的结果。
p45.en: Watching learning also occurs in non-human species, like a female cat taught her how to hunt. In fact, many important decisions that animals must make to survive — for example, what to eat, what to avoid, what to avoid, and how to find water — depend on observation and learning. This type of learning allows young animals to develop effective behaviour without potentially fatal trial error. The chimpanzees and crows learn to use leaves and branches to produce tools that facilitate the excavation of larvae and ants. In fact, many animal behaviour, whether human or non-human, is the result of observational learning.

p46.original: 一组巧妙的研究证明了恒河猴可以观察学习。在野外，恒河猴对蛇的反应是警觉和回避，但在实验室出生和长大的恒河猴并不害怕蛇，不过这只发生在研究人员向它们展示了一段野生恒河猴明显害怕蛇的视频之前。看完视频后，这些在实验室里长大的灵长类动物在好几个月内都会避开蛇（Galef & Laland，2005）。有趣的是，一项后续研究向实验室里的猴子展示了一段野生恒河猴似乎害怕花而不是蛇的视频，但在该研究中，实验室里的猴子并没有模仿害怕花的行为，这再次证明了我们的遗传倾向是对天然的生物威胁和捕食者做出快速反应。因此，观察学习具有适应环境的益处，换言之，它帮助我们生存。
p46.en: A clever study has shown that rhesus monkeys can observe learning. In the wild, the rhesus monkey reacts to snakes with vigilance and evasiveness, but the rhesus monkeys born and grown up in laboratories are not afraid of the snakes, but only before researchers showed them a video of wild rhesus monkeys apparently afraid of the snakes. After watching the video, these primates, who grew up in the lab, avoided snakes for months (Galef & Laland, 2005). Interestingly, a follow-up study showed monkeys in the lab a video of wild rheumatism that seemed afraid of flowers rather than snakes, but in that study, monkeys in the lab did not imitate fear of flowers, which proves once again that our genetic tendency is a rapid response to natural biological threats and predators. Thus, observational learning has the benefit of adapting to the environment, in other words, it helps us to survive.

p48.original: 正如你可能已经猜到的那样，许多关于观察学习的研究都会关注电影和视频中的暴力对于人的影响（Huesmann et al.，2003）。可想而知，这个问题会有争议，因为许多证据都只是相关性（correlational）的证据（Anderson & Bushman，2001）。尽管超过50项研究都表明观察暴力与暴力行为存在相关性，这是相当可靠的证据。但是，观察暴力会导致暴力行为吗？或者，也许因果是反过来的：是因为暴力的人会被暴力电影和视频所吸引吗？
p48.en: As you may have guessed, many studies on observational learning focus on the impact of violence in films and videos on people (Huesmann et al., 2003). It is conceivable that this issue will be controversial because many of the evidence is only evidence of relevance (Anderson & Bushman, 2001). Although more than 50 studies have shown the correlation between observing violence and violence, this is fairly reliable evidence. But is observing violence leading to violence? Or, perhaps, the cause and effect are the opposite: are violent people attracted to violent films and videos?

p49.original: 通过100多项实验研究，专家们现在知道，观察暴力确实会增加暴力行为的可能性（Huesmann & Moise，1996；Primavera & Herron，1996）。事实上，观看媒体暴力与随后的攻击行为之间的联系比含铅涂料与儿童智商之间的联系更强，几乎与吸烟和癌症之间的联系一样强（Bushman & Anderson，2001）。媒体暴力的观看者在随后观察到暴力行为时也表现出较少的情绪唤起和痛苦——这种类似于习惯化的状态被称为心理麻木（Murray & Kippax，1979）。心理学家艾略特·阿伦森（Elliot Aronson）认为，广泛的媒体暴力是导致暴力悲剧——例如，在学校和其他公共场所泛滥的枪击事件——的因素之一（Aronson，2000）。
p49.en: Through more than 100 experimental studies, experts now know that observing violence does increase the likelihood of violence (Huesmann & Moise, 1996); Primavera & Herron, 1996. In fact, the link between watching media violence and subsequent attacks is stronger than that between lead paint and children's IQ, almost as strong as that between smoking and cancer (Bushman & Anderson, 2001). Media violent viewers also show less emotional agitation and pain when they observe violence later — a state similar to custom known as mental numbness (Murray & Kippax, 1979). According to the psychologist Elliot Alonson, widespread media violence is one of the factors leading to the tragedy of violence — for example, shootings that are widespread in schools and other public places (Aronson, 2000).

p50.original: 这种影响也延伸到暴力视频游戏上。一项研究将大学生随机分配到15分钟的真人快打（Mortal Kombat）游戏或非暴力电子游戏中，随后测量了这些玩电子游戏的学生的攻击性行为，测量方式是，他们是否会向不喜欢辛辣食物的同学分发辣酱（获得辣酱的人一定要吞下）。果然，玩真人快打的学生比对照组更有可能分发辣酱，而且让接受者吞下了更多的辣酱（Barlett et al.，2009）。这项研究的相关研究发现，视频游戏中的暴力越逼真，攻击性情绪和唤醒的程度就越高（Barlett & Rodeheffer，2009）。当然，并非所有模仿都是糟糕的。多亏了模仿，我们还学会了慈善行为、安慰处于困境中的其他人，以及在道路合法的一侧上行驶。一般来说，人们通过观察他人会学到很多东西，既包括亲社会（帮助）行为，也包括反社会（伤害）行为。这种从观察中学习的能力使我们能够有效地习得行为，而无须经过烦琐的反复试错。因此，虽然观察学习是导致暴力行为的一个因素，但它也使我们能够通过从他人的错误和成功中获益，习得有用的社会行为。
p50.en: This influence extends to violent video games as well. A study randomly assigned university students to the Mortal Kombat game or non-violent video game for 15 minutes, then measured the aggressive behaviour of those students who played video games by measuring whether they would distribute spicy sauce to students who did not like spicy foods (those who had to swallow it). It is true that students who play real-person beats are more likely to distribute hot sauce than control teams and to swallow more hot sauce (Barlett et al., 2009). The study found that the more violence in video games becomes real, the more aggressive and awakening it is (Barlett & Rodeheffer, 2009). Of course, not all imitations are bad. Thanks to the imitation, we have learned to be charitable, to comfort others in distress, and to travel on the legitimate side of the road. In general, people learn a lot by looking at others, both pro-social (help) behaviour and anti-social (harm) behaviour. This ability to learn from observation enables us to learn behaviour effectively without the need to go through cumbersome and repeated trials. Thus, while observing learning is a factor that leads to violence, it also enables us to learn useful social behaviour by benefiting from the mistakes and successes of others.

p51.original: 4.10.3 观察学习在全球社会问题中的应用
p51.en: 4.10.3 Observe the application of learning in global social issues

p52.original: 电视是观察学习最重要的来源之一，其作用方式不只是带来我们刚刚提到的那种不可取的行为。在美国家庭里，通过观察学习，长期播放的儿童节目芝麻街（Sesame Street）使用大鸟（Big Bird）和饼干怪（Cookie Monster）等深受喜爱的角色教给儿童语言、算术和礼仪。在墨西哥，电视主管米格尔·萨比多（Miguel Sabido）特意借鉴了班杜拉的研究，创作了广受欢迎的肥皂剧《跟我来》（Ven Conmigo），该剧聚焦于通过扫盲班联系在一起的一群人。在第一季播出之后，播出区域的成年人扫盲班的入学人数猛增至上一年的九倍（Smith，2002b）。
p52.en: Television is one of the most important sources of observation and learning, not only by bringing about undesirable behaviour of the kind we have just mentioned. In the United States, through observational learning, the long-run children's programme Sesame Street teaches children language, arithmetic and protocol using such well-loved roles as Big Bird and Cookie Monster. In Mexico, Miguel Sabido, the television director, drew specifically on Bandura's research and created the popular soap opera " Ven Conmigo ", which focuses on a group of people linked through literacy classes. After the first season of broadcasts, the number of adult literacy classes in the broadcast areas increased sharply to nine times the previous year (Smith, 2002b).

p53.original: 这个思路被一个非营利组织——国际人口沟通组织（Populations Communications International）——所采纳，并在全球范围内推广。因此，电视剧现在的目标不仅在于扫盲，还在于促进妇女权利、安全性行为以及预防艾滋病毒和意外怀孕。此类节目广受欢迎，在拉丁美洲、非洲、南亚和东亚、中东、加勒比地区等地区拥有大量的粉丝（见图4-11）。在坦桑尼亚，他们了解到艾滋病是通过人而非蚊子传播的；在印度，这些节目质疑童婚的做法。在加勒比地区，肥皂剧倡导人类要对环境负责任。
p53.en: This idea has been adopted by a non-profit organization, Population Communications International, and has been replicated globally. Television dramas are therefore now aimed not only at literacy, but also at promoting women's rights, safe sex and the prevention of HIV and unwanted pregnancies. Such programmes are popular, with a large number of fans in Latin America, Africa, South and East Asia, the Middle East and the Caribbean (see figures 4-11). In Tanzania, they learned that AIDS is transmitted through people rather than through mosquitoes; In India, these programmes question the practice of child marriage. In the Caribbean, soap operas advocate for accountability of humanity to the environment.

p54.original: 图4-11 观察学习帮助解决现实世界的问题
p54.en: Figure 4-11 Observation of learning to help solve real-world problems

p55.original: 注：广告牌、电视节目和其他媒体活动可以成为促进社会变革的有效工具。当时，东非坦桑尼亚的这块广告牌，以及一部内容涉及对艾滋病的认识的流行广播剧，宣传了安全性行为和计划生育。
p55.en: Note: Billboards, television programmes and other media activities can be effective tools for social change. At that time, this billboard in East Africa and Tanzania, as well as a popular radio show on AIDS awareness, promoted safe sex and family planning.

p56.original: 这当真有效。一个在印度播出的肥皂剧使得全村人都签署了一封承诺书，承诺停止童婚。类似，坦桑尼亚人现在越来越赞成计划生育。在印度农村，女孩入学率上升了10%～38%。其他项目已经成功地提高了儿童免疫接种率、降低了艾滋病毒传播、增进了营养意识并敦促了戒烟。总体而言，电视似乎可以成为产生积极社会变革的一种手段，将心理学研究的成果辐射出去，对人们的生活产生重要影响（Naugle & Hornik，2014；Singhal & Rogers，2002）。
p56.en: It really works. A soap opera aired in India led to the signing of a promise by the entire village to end child marriage. Similarly, Tanzanians are now increasingly in favour of family planning. In rural India, the enrolment of girls increased by 10 to 38 per cent. Other projects have been successful in increasing child immunization rates, reducing HIV transmission, raising nutritional awareness and urging smoking cessation. In general, television seems to be a means of generating positive social change, by irradiating the results of psychological research and having an important impact on people's lives (Naogle & Hornik, 2014); Singhal & Rogers, 2002.

p57.original: 观察学习不仅是通过电视 不仅仅是电视可以促进社会变革并影响我们的行为。与他人讨论话题和行动也可以促使我们采取政治或社会行动，无论是传统的还是激进的。
p57.en: Watching learning isn't just television, it's not just television that can drive social change and influence our behavior. Discussion of topics and actions with others can also prompt us to take political or social action, whether traditional or radical.

p58.original: 一项研究首先向参与者提供了一些在小笼子里饲养产蛋鸡的阅读材料（这是动物权利活动家长期以来一直抗议的一个问题），然后告诉他们，尽管存在动物福利问题，许多人仍然会购买以这种方式养鸡的农场的鸡蛋。接下来，参与者阅读了一段文字内容，要么是提倡采取合法政治行动来制止这种做法，要么是提倡非法的、更激进的行动，如闯入农场释放鸡群。最后，参与者完成了问卷调查，调查询问了他们对该问题的关注程度，他们认为是否要让其他人意识到该问题的重要性，以及他们有多大可能为此参与政治或激进行动。不过，在完成调查问卷之前，一半的参与者有机会与一小群其他人就这些问题进行一些讨论。讨论是否会带来差别？
p58.en: A study first provided participants with reading materials for the production of egg chickens in small cages (an issue that animal rights activists have long protested) and then told them that, despite animal welfare problems, many people would still buy eggs from farms where chickens were raised in this way. The participants then read a text that either advocated legitimate political action to stop the practice or illegal and more radical action, such as breaking into farms and releasing chickens. Finally, the participants completed a questionnaire asking them about the extent of their interest in the issue, whether they thought it was important to make others aware of the importance of the issue and how likely they were to be involved in political or radical action to that end. However, before completing the questionnaire, half of the participants had the opportunity to discuss these issues with a small group of others. Does the discussion make a difference?

p59.original: 讨论的确会带来差别。研究人员发现，与在完成问卷之前未与他人讨论该主题的参与者相比，讨论组中的参与者对这些鸡表达了更大的关注，并且更愿意让其他人意识到这个问题。这种影响既适用于合法的政治行动，也适用于非法的激进行动；换言之，人们可能会同意并承诺执行该团体正在讨论的任何类型的行动，无论其是否合法。调查人员断言，结果支持这样一种观点：激进主义不是来自人格类型，而是更多地因为与志同道合的人接触而导致的（Thomas et al.，2014）。这项研究和其他类似的研究作为大量相关科学证据的一部分，证明了社会学习在人类行为中的重要性。
p59.en: The discussion does make a difference. Researchers found that participants in the discussion group expressed greater interest in the chickens than participants who had not discussed the subject with others before completing the questionnaire and were more willing to make others aware of the problem. This influence applies to both legitimate political and illegal radical action; In other words, one may agree and commit to carry out any type of action that the group is discussing, whether legal or not. Investigators have asserted that the result supports the view that radicalism does not stem from the type of personality, but rather from more contact with like-minded people (Thomas et al., 2014). This and other similar studies, as part of a wealth of relevant scientific evidence, demonstrate the importance of social learning in human behaviour.

p60.original: 4.11 大脑机制、学习和“高级”认知学习
p60.en: 4.11 Brain mechanisms, learning and “advanced” cognitive learning

p62.original: 审视参与学习的大脑过程。
p62.en: Look at the brain processes involved in learning.

p63.original: 现在我们很清楚，大学课堂所需的许多复杂和抽象的学习都与巴甫洛夫、华生和斯金纳所研究的学习有着根本的不同。例如，习得心理学领域的知识包括建立心理意象、吸收概念和思考它们之间的联系。并不是说行为的条件反射不参与人类学习，毕竟，学生们确实会为了成绩而努力，看到比萨时也会流口水；但行为学习的原理并不能解释整个“高级”认知学习。
p63.en: Now it is clear to us that many of the complex and abstract studies required in university classrooms are fundamentally different from those studied by Pavlov, Watson and Skinner. For example, knowledge in the area of psychology includes the creation of psychological images, the absorption of concepts and the reflection of the links between them. It is not that the conditions of behaviour are not reflected in human learning, that, after all, students do work for achievement, and they spit when they see pizza; But the principles of behavioral learning do not explain the whole concept of “advanced” cognitive learning.

p64.original: 接下来的章节将带我们更深入地了解认知学习这个领域，我们将讨论记忆、思维、概念形成、问题解决和智力。在那里，你将了解更多作为认知基础的心理结构。我们将面临的挑战正是行为主义者希望避免的挑战：在研究认知时，我们必须对无法直接测量的过程进行推断。然而，我们会发现，认知心理学家已经开发出非常巧妙的方法来获取客观数据，以此作为推理的基础。其中最新的是脑成像，它在过去十年左右全面上线；正如我们将看到的，它让心理学家近乎客观地窥见了私密的心理过程。
p64.en: The next chapter will provide us with a deeper understanding of the field of cognitive learning, where we will discuss memory, thinking, conceptualization, problem resolution and intelligence. There you will learn more about the psychological structure that underpins the cognitive base. The challenge we will face is precisely the challenge that activists want to avoid: in studying knowledge, we must extrapolate processes that cannot be directly measured. However, we will find that cognitive psychologists have developed very sophisticated methods to obtain objective data as a basis for reasoning. The most recent of these is brain imaging, which was fully online in the last decade or so; As we will see, it gives psychologists near-objective insight into the intimate psychological process.

p65.original: 迄今为止，我们对学习相关的生物学了解多少？在神经元层面上，学习涉及增强神经细胞群突触的物理变化，这一过程被称为长时程增强（long-term potentiation）（Antonova et al.，2001；Kandel，2000）。最初，参与学习任务的各个脑区的神经元都会非常努力地工作，例如，当一个人学习各种物体的位置时，视觉皮层（visual cortex）和顶叶皮层（parietal cortex）中的细胞可能会迅速放电。随着学习的进展，随着神经连接强度的增强，发放模式变得不那么强烈（Buchel et al.，1999）。神经通路用得越多，就会变得越强大、越密集。正如我们锻炼的肌肉群会变大一样，我们锻炼的神经通路也是如此；在某种程度上，学习对大脑的作用就像力量训练对身体的作用一样（Buchel et al.，1999）。
p65.en: So far, what do we know about learning about biology? At the neuron level, learning involves physical changes that enhance the synaptic contact of the neurocell population, a process known as long-term intensification (Antonova et al., 2001); Kandel, 2000. Initially, neurons in the various brain regions involved in the learning mission would work very hard, for example, cells in the visual cortex and parietal cortex may be discharged rapidly when a person learns the location of various objects. As learning progresses, the distribution pattern becomes less intense as the intensity of neural connections increases (Buchel et al., 1999). The more neuropaths are used, the more powerful and dense they become. Just as our muscles will grow, so will our neuropaths. To some extent, learning works for the brain as much as force training does for the body (Buchel et al., 1999).

p66.original: 我们还知道小脑（cerebellum）和边缘系统（limbic system）在习得性恐惧和条件性味觉厌恶等经典条件反应中至关重要（Miller，2004；Taub & Mintz，2010）。在操作性条件反射中，大脑的奖赏回路开始发挥作用，尤其是在额叶皮层（frontal cortex）和边缘系统富含多巴胺（dopamine）受体的部分区域（O’Doherty et al.，2004；Roesch & Olson，2004）。许多专家现在都相信大脑会使用这个回路来识别奖赏，即正强化的本质（Fiorillo et al.，2003；Kim et al.，2012；Shizgal & Arvanitogiannis，2003）。
p66.en: We also know that cerebellum and lmbic system are essential in the classic conditional response to sexual fear and odour aversion (Miller, 2004); Taub & Mintz, 2010. In operational reflections, the reward circuit of the brain begins to function, especially in the frontal cortex and in parts of the peripheral system rich in dopamine receptors (O'Doherty et al., 2004); Roech & Olson, 2004. Many experts now believe that the brain will use this circuit to identify the rewards, the reinforcing nature (Fiorillo et al., 2003); Kim et al., 2012; Shizgal & Arvanitugiannis, 2003.

p68.original: 虽然记住习得的联结和我们行为的后果对于我们的生存非常重要，但是遗忘那些不相干的联结也很重要。正如野生动物需要忘记干涸的水坑一样，你必须学会应对学校时间表或交通法规的变化。这些例子涉及先前习得的反应的消退。神经科学家发现，当某些神经递质（neurotransmitters）（包括谷氨酸盐和去甲肾上腺素）阻断记忆时，消退就会发生（Miller，2004；Travis，2004）。
p68.en: While it is important for our survival to remember the ties of learning and the consequences of our behaviour, it is also important to forget those unrelated links. Just as wildlife needs to forget dried-up water pits, you have to learn to cope with changes in school schedules or traffic regulations. These examples relate to the decline in the response previously acquired. Neuroscientists found that when certain neurotransmitters (including aromate and adrenaline) interrupt memories (Miller, 2004); Travis, 2004.

p69.original: 诸如此类的发现激发了人们对药物的研究，以达成从前只见于未来电影中的功效：阻断与某些特定事件相关的情绪创伤，这些事件包括战斗经历、暴力犯罪和可怕的事故等。最近的研究取得了初步成果（Kindt et al.，2009；Soeter & Kindt，2010）。实验者已经成功地消除了动物与人类被试对此类创伤事件的典型记忆的情绪唤醒。尽管这一非凡的发现对于治疗暴力犯罪、战争、事故和自然灾害的幸存者具有巨大的潜力，但这个快速发展的领域的未来方向仍然存在着伦理问题。
p69.en: Discoveries such as these have inspired research on drugs to achieve the efficacy that was previously seen only in future films: to disrupt emotional trauma associated with certain specific events, such as combat experiences, violent crimes and terrible accidents. Preliminary results of recent studies (Kindt et al., 2009); Seeter & Kindt, 2010. The experimenters have successfully eliminated the emotional awakening of the typical memory of such traumatic events that animals and humans have been tested. Although this extraordinary discovery has great potential for treating survivors of violent crime, war, accident and natural disasters, there are ethical issues about the future direction of this rapidly developing area.

p71.original: 在继续之前，让我们回到本章开头的问题：萨布拉对飞行的恐惧。
p71.en: Before proceeding, let us return to the question at the beginning of this chapter: Sabra's fear of flight.

p72.original: 心理学很有用 重温飞行恐惧

p73.original: 你认为萨布拉对飞行的厌恶背后是哪种学习，操作性条件反射还是经典条件反射？
p73.en: What kind of study do you think Sabra's aversion to flight is, operational or classic?

p74.original: 虽然我们可能永远无法知道一开始是什么导致了她的恐惧，但是我们猜测这两种形式的条件反射都牵涉其中。恐惧通常是来自涉及经典条件反射的亲身经历。或者，恐惧也可能来自观察学习，也许来自惊恐的父母或同伴。一旦恐惧被习得，操作性条件反射就可以维持它，因为人们在避开他们害怕的对象时获得了奖赏。
p74.en: While we may never know what caused her fear at first, we speculate that both forms of reflection are involved. Fear usually comes from personal experience involving the reflection of classic conditions. Alternatively, fear can also come from observational learning, perhaps from frightened parents or peers. Once fear is learned, operational reflexes sustain it, as people are rewarded for avoiding the objects they fear.

p75.original: 这些假定促使一些航空公司尝试一种被称为认知行为疗法的混合疗法，旨在帮助人们克服对飞行的恐惧。令人欣慰的是，萨布拉在会议开始前几周参加了其中一个治疗课程。她联系了航空公司，报名参加机场附近三个周末的课程学习。
p75.en: These assumptions have prompted some airlines to try a combination of therapy known as cognitive behaviour therapy, which is designed to help people overcome fear of flight. It is gratifying to note that Sabra attended one of the therapeutic courses several weeks before the start of the conference. She contacted the airline and enrolled for three weekend courses near the airport.

p76.original: 她如期而至，满怀期待和忐忑。
p76.en: She was on schedule, with expectations and frustrations.

p77.original: 治疗师会探究她的童年经历和幻想吗？
p77.en: Will the therapist explore her childhood and fantasy?

p79.original: 或者，她是否必须经历某种吓人的治疗，例如，在小型飞机上倒挂飞行？
p79.en: Or does she have to go through some kind of intimidating treatment, for example, upside-down flights on small aircraft?

p80.original: 事实证明，她最糟糕的担忧是毫无根据的。一位行为心理学家组织了治疗课程，将九名参与者汇聚在一个小会议室中。他先解释说，这种恐惧是习得的，就像你在医生那里看到针头时可能学会了畏缩一样。不过，因为恐惧的起源并不重要，这个飞行恐惧课程将关注现在，而不是过去。萨布拉开始觉得轻松多了。
p80.en: Her worst fears have proved unfounded. A behavioural psychologist organized a therapeutic course bringing together nine participants in a small conference room. He explained first that the fear was learned, as you might learn when you saw a needle at a doctor's office. However, because the origin of fear is not important, this flight fear course will focus on the present, not on the past. Sabra is starting to feel much easier.

p81.original: 基于条件反射的治疗课程结合了多种学习策略。采用经典条件反射，通过逐渐增加她的飞行经历来消除她的恐惧。运用操作性条件反射使治疗师和小组其他成员的正强化发挥作用。此外，认知学习部分将帮助她更多地去了解飞机的工作原理。
p81.en: The treatment curriculum, which is condition-based, combines a variety of learning strategies. Using classic reflections, her fear was overcome by gradually increasing her flight experience. The application of operational reflections is enabling the therapist and other members of the team to perform their role. In addition, the cognitive learning component will help her to learn more about the workings of the aircraft.

p82.original: 通过认知行为疗法，萨布拉学会了用新的方式看待飞行体验。逐渐接触飞行也有助于消除她的恐惧反应，这被称为脱敏（消退的一种形式）。
p82.en: Through cognitive behaviour therapy, Sabra has learned to view flight experiences in new ways. Gradually exposed flight also helps to eliminate her fear response, which is called dissensitization (a form of retreat).

p83.original: 在简要概述了他们的课程之后，该小组参观了机场，包括停在停机坪上的一架客机的机舱。然后他们回到会议室，了解飞行员如何控制飞机，学习在物理学上飞机如何保持空中飞行的物理原理。该小组还观看了一些商业喷气式飞机的日常飞行视频。总而言之，第一堂课进行得很顺利，大家都显得比刚开始的时候轻松了许多。
p83.en: Following a brief overview of their courses, the team visited the airport, including the cabin of a passenger aircraft parked on the apron. They then returned to the conference room to learn how pilots controlled the aircraft and learned how to maintain the physical principles of air flight in physics. The team also watched some daily flight videos of commercial jets. In conclusion, the first lesson went well, and everyone seemed much easier than they had been at the beginning.

p84.original: 第二个周末以更多的课堂讨论开始。然后，全班同学回到飞机上，在那里坐下并进行了一系列放松练习，旨在消除参与者的恐惧，并学习对坐飞机产生一种新的更放松的反应。这种训练包括深呼吸和全身特定肌肉群的渐进放松。当小组中的每个人都报告感到放松时，他们再次在飞机的电视显示屏上观看飞行视频。随后是更多的放松练习。第二个周末的最后一项活动是启动引擎和经历正式飞行前的流程，以及更多的放松练习。
p84.en: The second weekend began with more classroom discussions. The class then returned to the plane, where they sat and conducted a series of relaxing exercises aimed at removing the fear of the participants and learning to produce a new, more relaxed response to flying. This training includes deep breathing and gradual relaxation of specific muscle groups throughout the body. When everyone in the group reported a sense of relaxation, they again watched the flight video on the television screen of the aircraft. Then there's more relaxing practice. The last event on the second weekend was the start-up of the engine and the process prior to the official flight, as well as more exercises to relax.

p85.original: 最后一个周末的课程与上一次几乎相同。唯一的区别是这次课程包含一次实际的飞行，这是一次20分钟的短途旅行，经过当地乡村然后返回机场。这当然是自愿的，但班上九个人中只有一个选择不去。萨布拉去了，虽然仍有一丝焦虑。不过，治疗师鼓励小组成员专注于他们学到的放松练习，而不是他们的恐惧感。令所有参与者惊讶的是，这些技术帮助他们完成了飞行练习而不至于情绪失控。虽然大家的恐惧没有完全消失，但飞机上的每个人都能够控制住恐惧。
p85.en: The last weekend was almost the same as the last. The only difference is that the course included a physical flight, a 20-minute short trip through the local village and then back to the airport. Of course it is voluntary, but only one of the nine in the class has a choice. Sabra went, although there was still a little anxiety. However, the therapists encouraged the members of the team to focus on the relaxing exercises they had learned, rather than on their fear. To the surprise of all participants, these technologies helped them to complete their flight exercises and not lose their temper. While the fear of everyone has not completely disappeared, everyone on board can control it.

p86.original: 最令人高兴的是，萨布拉能够参加夏威夷的会议了。顺便一提，她的会开得富有成效，她在夏威夷也度过了一段美好的时光。我们还注意到，她从那时到现在已经飞行了好几次。她说，每次旅行都会变得更容易一些，正如有关学习的心理学所预测的那样。
p86.en: It is most gratifying that Sabra has been able to attend the Hawaiian conference. By the way, her meeting was very productive and she had a good time in Hawaii. We also note that she has flown several times since then. She said that each trip would become easier, as the psychology of learning had predicted.

p87.original: 批判性思维的应用：不同的人有不同的“学习风格”吗
p87.en: Application of critical thinking: Do different people have different “learning styles”?

p88.original: 人们的学习方式无疑有所不同。正如通过观察你的同学你所能看到的，每个人都会带着不同的兴趣、能力、气质因素、发展水平、社会经验和情绪来承担学习任务。但我们能说这些差异形成了不同的“学习风格”吗？例如，是否有些人是“视觉学习者”，需要看到学习资料而不是听到学习资料，而“听觉学习者”也许必须听到学习资料？
p88.en: There is no doubt that people learn differently. As you can see from the observation of your classmates, everyone has a different interest, ability, quality factor, level of development, social experience and emotions to take on the task of learning. But can we say that these differences create a different “learning style”? For example, are there people who are “visual learners” who need to see rather than hear learning materials, and “hearing learners” may have to hear learning materials?

p89.original: 教育工作者被学习风格的概念所吸引，希望通过因材施教来鼓励学习。对学习风格的热切关注又进而导致学习风格量表激增，每个量表都旨在诊断某个学生如何学习最好，从而告诉我们如何订制适合每个学习者的教学环境。也许你参加过这样的测试。但这些传言是基于事实还是基于幻想？
p89.en: Educators are attracted to the concept of learning styles and wish to encourage learning by teaching them for their own reasons. A keen interest in learning styles, in turn, leads to a proliferation of learning style tables, each designed to diagnose how a student learns best, and thus to tell us how to customize the teaching environment for each learner. Maybe you've taken a test like this. But are these rumors based on facts or on illusions?

p91.original: 从批判的角度来看，关键问题在于“学习风格”的含义。这个词似乎不言自明，但每个人理解的意思是否一致？学习风格到底是要求还仅仅是偏好某种学习方式？换言之，如果你是一个“视觉学习者”，当视觉不可用时，这在多大程度上真正影响了你的学习能力？学习风格是否一成不变（如同眼睛的颜色），还是人们可以调整他们的学习方法，以适应不同的主题（例如，文学、心理学、牙科或音乐）的需要？
p91.en: From a critical point of view, the key issue is the meaning of “learning style”. That word seemed self-evident, but was everyone's understanding consistent? Is learning style a requirement or is it just a way of learning? In other words, if you are a “vision learner”, to what extent does this really affect your learning ability when the vision is not available? Is the learning style static (like the colour of the eye) or can people adapt their learning methods to different themes (e.g. literature, psychology, dentistry or music)?

p92.en: What are the sources of the view?

p93.original: 不幸的是，大多数关于学习风格的出版物的作者都没有进行支持其主张所需的对照研究（Rohrer & Pashler，2012；Stahl，1999）。相反，他们所说的支持他们主张的“研究”多未发表，因此我们无法让教学和学习的专家进行评判或审查。发表和评论研究及其结果是科学方法的一个关键步骤。避开这一要求可能是一种警示，表明提出主张的人已屈从于一种或多种偏见，因而缺乏可信度。
p93.en: Unfortunately, most authors of learning-style publications have not carried out the comparative research needed to support their claims (Rohrer & Pashler, 2012); Stahl, 1999. Rather, the “research” they call in support of their claims has been largely unpublished, and we are therefore unable to allow for evaluation or review by teaching and learning specialists. To publish and comment on research and its results as a key step in scientific approaches. Avoiding this requirement may be a warning that the person making the claim has surrendered to one or more prejudices and thus lacks credibility.

p95.original: 我们在审视学习风格的证据时遇到的一个问题是，即使在学习风格的狂热者中，我们也没有找到其一致认同的不同学习风格的列表。尽管教育工作者经常谈论“语言学习者”“视觉学习者”和“动觉（运动）学习者”，但一些量表还提出了以下风格的某种组合：触觉（触碰）、逻辑、社交、孤独、主动/反思、感知/直觉、思考/感觉、判断/知觉、序列/全局。这种关于“学习风格”基本类别的广泛分歧应该引起批判性思考者的注意，这表明关于学习风格的主张可能仅基于推测和常识，而不是真正的科学发现。
p95.en: One of the problems we encounter when looking at evidence of learning styles is that even among the fanatics of learning styles, we do not find a list of different learning styles that they agree to. Although educators often talk about “language learners”, “vision learners” and “motion learners”, some tables also suggest a combination of touch (touching), logic, socialization, isolation, initiative/reflection, perception/intitude, thinking/favorite, judgement/sensitization, sequence/globalization. This wide divergence of views on the basic categories of “learning style” should be brought to the attention of critical thinkers, which suggests that ideas of learning style may be based only on speculation and common sense, not on real scientific discoveries.

p96.original: 当我们审视证据时，我们看到的第二个也是更麻烦的危险信号是，没有什么发现支持个体的学习风格与其实际学习（绩效）之间存在关系。事实上，大多数学习风格的倡导者几乎都没有数据来支持他们的主张——不同分数的人以不同的方式学习相同的资料。事实上，已有的研究表明，将教学环境与一个人声称的学习方式相匹配几乎不会影响其成绩。因此，对学习风格的更准确解释可能是，它们反映了偏好而非必须采用某种学习方式（Krätzig & Arbuthnott，2006）。
p96.en: As we look at the evidence, the second and more troubling dangerous signal we see is that there is little to find that there is a relationship between the learning style that supports individuals and their actual learning (performance). In fact, the majority of learning-style advocates have little data to support their claim — people with different scores learn the same information in different ways. Indeed, existing studies have shown that matching the teaching environment with a person's alleged learning style will hardly affect his or her performance. Therefore, a more precise explanation of learning styles may be that they reflect preference rather than the need for some form of learning (Krätzig & Arbutthnott, 2006).

p97.original: 是否需要从多元化的视角
p97.en: Is there a need for a pluralistic perspective?

p98.original: 如果学习风格确实存在，跨文化视角能否帮助我们理解它们（Winerman，2006b）？尼斯贝特（Nisbett，2003）和其他研究人员的研究表明，亚洲人与美国人对世界的看法往往截然不同，美国人专注于最重要的物体，而亚洲人则更加关注全局。（是文化上的而不是生理上的差异：亚裔美国人的感知方式与其他美国人基本相同。）为了说明这两种“观看”风格的差异，请看下页图中以丛林为背景的老虎。尼斯贝特的研究组发现，典型的美国人会花费更多的精力将场景的突出元素——老虎——归入逻辑类别，而亚洲人通常更关注情境和背景——丛林。
p98.en: If learning styles do exist, can cross-cultural perspectives help us understand them (Winerman, 2006b)? Nisbett, 2003 and other researchers have shown that Asians and Americans tend to see the world differently, with Americans focusing on the most important objects, while Asians are more concerned with the whole picture. (Cultural rather than biological differences: Asian Americans feel the same way as other Americans. In order to illustrate the difference between these two “watch” styles, please see the tigers in the context of the jungle in the next page. The Nisbeth study team found that typical Americans would spend more effort on categorizing the salient elements of the scene — tigers — into the logical category, while Asians were usually more concerned with situations and contexts — the jungle.

p99.original: 文化也会影响人们进行课堂学习的方式。例如，美国人普遍认为学业成功来自先天智力，而东亚的文化则强调纪律和勤奋（Li，2005）。你认为哪种信仰体系可能会鼓励大多数孩子在学校表现出色？
p99.en: Culture also affects the way people learn in the classroom. For example, while Americans are generally of the opinion that academic success comes from congenital intelligence, East Asian cultures emphasize discipline and diligence (Li, 2005). What belief system do you think would encourage most children to perform well in school?

p100.original: 出生于韩国的心理学家金希荣（Heejung Kim）表示，其他文化差异也会影响学业成绩。在她的韩国教育经历中，需要小组讨论的课程很少见。在她经历过对小组讨论课程的苦苦挣扎后，金希荣（Kim，2002）决定寻找亚洲人和美国人在处理学术任务方式之间的差异。正如她所预测的那样，当亚洲的大学生和美国大学生需要解决问题时，美国人通常会从讨论问题的过程中受益，而这种讨论往往会抑制亚洲学生解决问题的能力。
p100.en: Heejung Kim, a psychologist born in Korea, said that other cultural differences could also affect academic achievement. In her Korean educational experience, there were few courses that required panel discussions. After she had struggled with the panel discussion, Kim 2002 decided to look for a difference between Asians and Americans in the way they handled academic missions. As she had predicted, when Asian and American students needed to solve problems, Americans often benefited from the process of discussing problems, which tended to inhibit the ability of Asian students to solve problems.

p101.original: 然而，我们发现，这些文化差异不是当前关于“学习风格”的辩论的一部分，因而没有包含在各种机构推销的任何一种学习风格量表中。但是我们在这里提到了它们，想说明的是，当前基于流行观点的想法（诸如学习风格对绩效的影响）可以通过接受科学界的批评并利用批评来改进理论以获得可信度。在这种情况下，学习风格的倡导者最好进行对照测试，以研究其中一些文化差异是否会带来实际绩效的差异。如果是，则可以创建真正反映实证（empirical）差异的学习风格类别。
p101.en: However, we find that these cultural differences are not part of the current debate on “learning styles” and are therefore not included in any of the learning styles schedules marketed by various institutions. But we mention them here to illustrate that current ideas based on popular views (such as the impact of learning styles on performance) can gain credibility by accepting criticism from the scientific community and using criticism to improve theory. In such cases, it is advisable for the proponents of learning styles to conduct a comparative test to see whether some of these cultural differences will lead to differences in actual performance. If so, a learning style category that truly reflects empirical differences can be created.

p102.original: 我们能够得出什么结论？

p103.original: 总体来说，虽然我们应该谨慎地看待大多数关于学习风格的主张，但是我们应该对新的进展保持开放的态度，包括那些可能来自跨文化研究的进展。除此之外，我们应该承认，对学习风格的兴趣促使教师和教授们在课堂上通过多媒体教学和各种“主动学习”技术来进行课堂教学。此外，现有研究表明，每个人都会学得更好，如果他们可以通过多种方式——既有视觉也有语言，还有动手学习——获得同样的资源的话（McKeachie，1990，1997，1999）。
p103.en: In general, while we should look carefully at most ideas about learning style, we should remain open to new developments, including those that may come from cross-cultural research. In addition, we should acknowledge that interest in learning styles has encouraged teachers and professors to teach in the classroom through multimedia teaching and various “active learning” techniques. In addition, existing research shows that everyone will learn better if they can access the same resources in a variety of ways — both visual and linguistic — as well as hands-on learning (McKeachie, 1990, 1997, 1999).

p104.original: 再回到我们的要点：我们建议谨慎解释旨在确定你的学习风格的测试结果。当心那些跟你说你是视觉型学习者、反思型学习者或其他类型学习者的人。
p104.en: And back to our point: we suggest a careful explanation of the test results aimed at determining your learning style. Beware those who tell you you're a visual learner, a reflective learner or other type of learner.

p105.original: 例如，仅仅因为你更喜欢图像而不是文字，并不意味着你应该避免阅读而只看图片。这种想法错误地认为每个人只能以一种方式学习。不过，你可以尝试其他学习策略。例如，如果视觉图像有助于你学习，则创建概念图；或者，如果反复听课有助于你学习，则录制讲座，但你仍然需要阅读指定的材料。
p105.en: For example, just because you prefer images rather than words does not mean you should avoid reading and just look at pictures. It is a misperception that everyone can only learn in one way or another. But you can try other learning strategies. For example, if visual images help you learn, create a concept map; Or, if repeated lessons help you to learn, you can record a lecture, but you still need to read the specified material.

p106.original: 看看这幅老虎的图片。你看到图片的哪些部分？观看图片时，你的视线会移动到哪里？尼斯贝特的团队发现，美国人会花更多的时间观察老虎和其他突出目标（例如，树和老虎的周围环境），而亚洲人则会花更多时间查看情境和背景的细节。
p106.en: Look at this picture of the tiger. What part of the picture do you see? Where will your sight move when you look at the picture? Nesbett's team found that Americans spend more time watching tigers and other prominent targets (e.g., the surroundings of trees and tigers), while Asians spend more time looking at the situation and context details.

p107.original: 关于学习风格的另一个问题是，它错误地认为我们的学习方式是固定不变的。然而，事实上，我们需要学习如何使我们的学习方式适合要学习的资源类型：你总不会以学习数学的方式来学习音乐。举例而言，学习涉及许多因素的相互作用：学习者、资源、展示资源的媒介、展示的组织、教师和学习者的个性以及学习的环境。到目前为止，你在心理学方面的学习已经向你展示了我们的大脑是多么具有适应性，通过改变连接来吸纳新的体验。因此，我们鼓励你尝试尽可能多的学习方式，毕竟，这是大学经历所提供的绝佳机会之一。
p107.en: Another problem with learning style is that it wrongly believes that our learning methods are static. In fact, however, we need to learn how to adapt our learning style to the type of resources to be learned: you never learn music in math. For example, learning involves many interactions: learners, resources, the media that showcase resources, the organization that showcases them, the personality of teachers and learners, and the learning environment. So far, your study of psychology has shown you how adaptable our brains are to absorb new experiences by changing connections. We therefore encourage you to try as many ways of learning as possible, which, after all, is one of the great opportunities offered by university experience.

p108.original: 试一试 调整自己以更好地学习
p108.en: Try and adjust yourself to learn better.

p109.original: 大多数学生都希望提高他们在某一门或多门课程中的表现。与其在学习风格的伪科学（pseudoscience）上浪费时间，不如尝试将经典条件反射和操作性条件反射的原则应用于帮助你设计能实现目标的计划。请使用本章迄今为止学过的各种原则，设计你自己的改变行为计划。
p109.en: Most students want to improve their performance in one or more of the courses. Instead of wasting time on learning style pseudoscience, try to apply the principles of classic and operational reflexes to help you design plans that will achieve your goals. Use the principles learned so far in this chapter to design your own behavioural change plan.

p110.original: 首先，确定某个特定的行为。不要设定类似获得更好的成绩这样的宽泛目标，而是让你的目标具体化，如每天阅读八页教科书或者每天复习课堂笔记。然后，根据经典条件反射和操作性条件反射的原则，确定至少五种可以促进新行为的方法。你可以从确定一种你想要与理想行为相关联的感觉或生物刺激开始，并找出一种通过经典条件反射来实现这一目标的方法。稍后，试图找出一两个你可以使用的强化物，最初连续使用。接下来，决定在你成功地开始塑造行为之后你将实施什么样的强化程序，并在此基础上写下你接受强化物的频率和类型。为了获得最佳效果，请将各种强化物用于多种强化程序，以保持自己的良好反应。那么开始吧！跟踪你的进度，并根据需要进行调整。
p110.en: First, to identify a particular act. Rather than setting broad goals like better results, it is making your goals concrete, such as reading eight pages of textbooks per day or reviewing classroom notes per day. Then, based on the principles of classic and operational reflexes, at least five methods are identified that can facilitate new behaviour. You can start by identifying a feeling or biostimulation that you want to be associated with ideal behaviour, and finding a way to achieve this through classic reflections. Later on, trying to find one or two of the reinforcements you can use, initially in continuous use. And then, to decide what kind of enhanced procedure you're going to apply after you have successfully begun shaping your behavior, and on that basis write down the frequency and type of reinforcements you're going to accept. In order to achieve optimal results, various enhancements are used in multiple enhancements to maintain their own good response. Then let's do it! Keep track of your progress and adjust as needed.
